26-md01b-qb-2374.solution: Scale 1:50 means real size = model size × 50. So the true height = 40 cm × 50 = 2,000 cm, which is 20 m.
26-md01b-qb-2374.trick: 50 is half of 100, so 40 × 50 is half of 4,000, which is 2,000 cm. Drop two zeros for metres: 20 m.

26-md01b-qb-2383.solution: The petrol use is steady, so distance is in proportion to litres. 240 km ÷ 20 L = 12 km per litre. So 35 L × 12 km/L = 420 km.
26-md01b-qb-2383.trick: 35 ÷ 20 = 7/4. A quarter of 240 is 60, and 7 × 60 = 420 km.

26-md01b-qb-2393.solution: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity. v = 3t² − 6t, so a = dv/dt = 6t − 6. At t = 2: a = 6(2) − 6 = 12 − 6 = 6 m/s².
26-md01b-qb-2393.trick: Differentiate in your head: 3t² becomes 6t and −6t becomes −6. At t = 2 that is 12 − 6 = 6.

26-md01b-qb-2401.solution: (f ∘ g)(x) means f(g(x)), so g is applied first. g(x) = 2x, so f(2x) = 2x + 3. The answer is 2x + 3.
26-md01b-qb-2401.trick: Read it as f of g: double x first, then add 3. The 3 comes last, so it is not doubled.

26-md01b-qb-2413.solution: As worded, a 45° angle of depression to the base does not match a 30 m roof and a 40 m gap. Reading the 45° as the angle of elevation from the roof to the top of the taller building, the rise above the roof = 40 × tan 45° = 40 × 1 = 40 m. So the extra height is 40 m.
26-md01b-qb-2413.trick: tan 45° = 1, so the rise equals the run: 40 m across means 40 m up.
26-md01b-qb-2413.computed: 40 m (reading 45° as the angle of elevation to the top of the taller building)
26-md01b-qb-2413.comment: As worded the numbers do not fit: from a 30 m roof, 40 m away, the angle of depression to the base is about 37° (arctan of 30 ÷ 40), not 45°. The show's 40 m only works if 45° is the angle of elevation to the top of the taller building, giving 40 × tan 45° = 40 m above the roof.

26-md01b-qb-2506.solution: Energy needed = work done against the weight = force × distance. The weight is already a force, so W = 10 N × 6 m = 60 J.
26-md01b-qb-2506.trick: Weight is already in newtons, so energy is weight × height: 10 × 6 = 60 J. No need for g.

26-md01b-qb-2514.solution: For z = 1 + i, the real part is 1 and the imaginary part is 1. The argument is θ = arctan(1 ÷ 1) = arctan 1 = 45°. The point (1, 1) is in the first quadrant, so θ = 45°.
26-md01b-qb-2514.trick: The real and imaginary parts are equal, so the point sits on the 45° diagonal.

26-md01b-qb-2518.solution: Multiply the matching components and add. A · B = (3)(1) + (4)(−2) = 3 − 8 = −5.
26-md01b-qb-2518.trick: Multiply the i parts and the j parts: 3 × 1 = 3 and 4 × (−2) = −8. Then 3 − 8 = −5. The minus sign from the j parts is the one to watch.

26-md01b-qb-2528.solution: The man, his shadow and the sun's ray make a right angled triangle. At 90° the sun would be directly overhead and there would be no shadow. Here tan θ = height ÷ shadow length = 1, so θ = 45°.
26-md01b-qb-2528.trick: Shadow equal to height means the two short sides are equal, so it is a 45° triangle. At 60° the shadow would be shorter than the man, and at 90° there is no shadow.

26-md01b-qb-2532.solution: Area = ∫ from 1 to 5 of (3x + 1) dx = [1.5x² + x] from 1 to 5. At x = 5 this is 37.5 + 5 = 42.5, and at x = 1 it is 1.5 + 1 = 2.5. The area is 42.5 − 2.5 = 40.
26-md01b-qb-2532.trick: The graph is a straight line, so area = width × height at the midpoint. At x = 3, y = 10, and the width is 4, so 40.

26-md01b-qb-2543.solution: Use the units asked for: 1.2 m = 120 cm and 8.4 kg = 8,400 g. Mass per cm = 8,400 g ÷ 120 cm = 70 g/cm.
26-md01b-qb-2543.trick: 8.4 ÷ 1.2 = 7 kg per metre. That is 7,000 g over 100 cm, so 70 g per cm.

26-md01b-qb-2553.solution: The amount halves each day. After 3 days it has halved 3 times, so the fraction left is (1/2)³ = 1/8.

26-md01b-qb-2557.solution: On a frictionless slope, only the component of gravity along the slope speeds the box up. So a = g sin θ = 9.8 × sin 30° = 9.8 × 0.5 = 4.9 m/s².
26-md01b-qb-2557.trick: sin 30° = 1/2, so the acceleration is half of g: 9.8 ÷ 2 = 4.9 m/s².

26-md01b-qb-2565.solution: Ohm's law: V = IR, so I = V ÷ R. I = 24 V ÷ 8 Ω = 3 amperes.
26-md01b-qb-2565.trick: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. Voltage divided by resistance gives the current.

26-md01b-qb-2571.solution: Scale 1:250 means real length = model length × 250. So 6 cm × 250 = 1,500 cm, which is 15 m.
26-md01b-qb-2571.trick: Each model centimetre is 250 cm = 2.5 m in real life, so 6 × 2.5 = 15 m.

26-md01b-qb-2577.solution: Ratio of B to A = B ÷ A = (5/8) ÷ (3/5). Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its flip, so (5/8) × (5/3) = 25/24. The ratio is 25:24.
26-md01b-qb-2577.trick: Put both over 40: 3/5 = 24/40 and 5/8 = 25/40. The ratio of B to A is just 25:24.

26-md01b-qb-2591.solution: bpm means beats per minute, which is a rate, so the total over 45 minutes is a count of beats. Total beats = rate × time = 140 × 45 = 6,300 beats.
26-md01b-qb-2591.trick: 140 × 45 is 14 × 45 with a zero added. 14 × 45 = 560 + 70 = 630, so the answer is 6,300.
26-md01b-qb-2591.comment: The value 6,300 is right, but bpm means beats per minute, which is a rate. Over 45 minutes the total is a count, so the unit should be beats, not bpm.

26-md01b-qb-2601.solution: Sugar is 4/6 of 120 L = 80 L and water is 40 L. Adding water leaves the sugar at 80 L. A 2:4 ratio needs the water to be double the sugar, which is 160 L. Water to add = 160 − 40 = 120 L.
26-md01b-qb-2601.trick: Sugar stays at 80 L. For 2:4 the water must be twice that, 160 L. It is 40 L now, so add 120 L.

26-md01b-qb-2611.solution: Critical points are where f'(x) = 0. f(x) = x³ − 3x², so f'(x) = 3x² − 6x = 3x(x − 2). This is zero at x = 0 and x = 2.
26-md01b-qb-2611.trick: Differentiate to 3x² − 6x, then factor out 3x: 3x(x − 2). The roots 0 and 2 read straight off.

26-md01b-qb-2621.solution: Work = power × time. 5 minutes = 300 s, so W = 400 W × 300 s = 120,000 J.
26-md01b-qb-2621.trick: 5 minutes is 300 s. 4 × 3 = 12, then add the four zeros from 400 and 300: 120,000 J.

26-md01b-qb-2645.solution: R(x) = 640x − 20x² is a downward parabola, so revenue is greatest at the vertex. x = −b ÷ (2a) = −640 ÷ (−40) = 16. Check: R'(x) = 640 − 40x = 0 gives x = 16.
26-md01b-qb-2645.trick: Factor it: R = 20x(32 − x), which is zero at x = 0 and x = 32. The peak is halfway between: 16.

26-md01b-qb-2656.solution: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity. v = 4t² − 12t + 9, so a = 8t − 12. At t = 2: a = 16 − 12 = 4 m/s².
26-md01b-qb-2656.trick: Differentiate: 4t² gives 8t, −12t gives −12, and the 9 vanishes. At t = 2: 16 − 12 = 4.

26-md01b-qb-2666.solution: The vertical component is magnitude × sin θ, with θ measured from the horizontal. So the vertical component = 25 × sin 90° = 25 × 1 = 25.
26-md01b-qb-2666.trick: A direction of 90° points straight up, so all 25 is vertical.

26-md01b-qb-2674.solution: Velocity is the integral of acceleration: v = ∫12t dt = 6t² + C. Since v = 0 at t = 0, C = 0. At t = 6: v = 6 × 6² = 6 × 36 = 216 units.
26-md01b-qb-2674.trick: 12t integrates to 6t², with no constant. At t = 6 that is 6 × 6 × 6 = 216.

26-md01b-qb-2684.solution: Assuming Hardy Weinberg equilibrium, a recessive trait shows only in people with two recessive alleles, so q² = 9% = 0.09. The recessive allele frequency is q = √0.09 = 0.3, which is 30%.
26-md01b-qb-2684.trick: The trait frequency is q², so take the square root: √0.09 = 0.3 because 3 × 3 = 9.

26-md01b-qb-2690.solution: The 200 mL holds 10% × 200 = 20 mL of solute, and adding water does not change that. For 4%, the total volume V satisfies 0.04 × V = 20, so V = 500 mL. Water added = 500 − 200 = 300 mL.
26-md01b-qb-2690.trick: The solute stays the same, so the volume grows by 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 times. 200 × 2.5 = 500 mL, so add 300 mL.

26-md01b-qb-2700.solution: P(x) = −x² + 20x − 36 is a downward parabola, so the maximum is at x = −b ÷ (2a) = −20 ÷ (−2) = 10. P(10) = −100 + 200 − 36 = 64.
26-md01b-qb-2700.trick: With −x² the peak is at half of the x coefficient, so x = 10. Then −100 + 200 − 36 = 64.

26-md01b-qb-2708.solution: Cost is the integral of marginal cost: C(x) = ∫(3x + 2) dx = 1.5x² + 2x, taking the fixed cost as zero. So C(8) = 1.5 × 64 + 2 × 8 = 96 + 16 = 112.
26-md01b-qb-2708.trick: Marginal cost rises in a straight line, so total cost = items × average MC. MC(0) = 2 and MC(8) = 26, so the average is 14, and 8 × 14 = 112.

26-md01b-qb-2716.solution: Car B's speed = 300 km ÷ 4 h = 75 km/h. Car A's speed is 4/5 of Car B's, so 4/5 × 75 = 60 km/h.
26-md01b-qb-2716.trick: Car B does 300 ÷ 4 = 75. One part of the ratio is 75 ÷ 5 = 15, so Car A is 4 × 15 = 60.

26-md01b-qb-2730.solution: The mass halves every 3 hours, so 12 hours gives 12 ÷ 3 = 4 halvings. Mass = 200 × (1/2)⁴ = 200 ÷ 16 = 12.5 g.
